subject: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files
parts: The user code needs to be in server.R or ui.R or global.R. To be modular and assist in maintenance, it is nice to have short source files. Is it possible to have the code in multiple R files with filenames that I choose, if the application will have lots of functions, such as to calculate various numerical summaries of the data ? Something like the Collate field of the DESCRIPTION file of typical R packages, perhaps ? I suppose it is possible to have many source function calls at the beginning of server.R, but could there be a neater way ?

messages.subject: Re: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Re: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files
parts: That should not be necessary, because it makes the application code harder to maintain. I was asking about having multiple smaller files, one for each function, which is good programming style. It seems that Shiny was designed with small applications that don't perform much processing in mind.

messages.author: b54054e5796fe6b4

parts: Try source (path,'local') it interprets the source as being inline where the statement executes

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Re: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files
parts: That's nice, because it doesn't add functions to the user's workspace, but I think that the R files shouldn't need to be explicitly sourced by the application developer.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Application Functions in Multiple Source Files
parts:
I strongly disagree that one file per function is a desirable style, but to each his/her own, I suppose! A good IDE or text editor makes it very easy to jump between functions regardless of where they are (Ctrl-. In RStudio, Ctrl-P in Sublime Text).

How about having a folder in your app dir called e.g. "helpers" and then a single call in your server.R or whatever that sources everything in that directory?
